Begin by noticing where your body touches the chair, bed or floor. Let it hold you.
[pause 46]
This practice builds awareness of tension and calm in your body. It is done fully clothed, simply sitting or lying down.
[pause 45]
Imagine a scale from zero to ten for how activated your body feels right now, where zero is completely calm.
Give yourself a number. There's no right answer.
[pause 48]
Notice the signs that tell you: your breathing, your heart rate, tension in your belly, buttocks and pelvic floor.
[pause 48]
Now let's practise bringing the number down.
[repeat 9]
[in 4] Breathe in slowly
[out 7] Breathe out, and let your body soften
[/repeat]
Check your number again. Has it changed, even a little?
[pause 48]
Now gently squeeze the pelvic floor for a moment, and notice how that tension feels.
[squeeze 3] Squeeze
[release 5] And let it go completely. Notice the difference.
[pause 46]
Practise the drop: as you breathe in, let the pelvic floor soften and lower.
[repeat 4]
[in 4] Breathe in, let it drop
[out 6] Breathe out, settle
[/repeat]
Imagine a moment when you felt yourself getting tense and rushed. Notice the number climb.
[pause 48]
Now use your breath and the drop to bring it back down, staying with the scene.
[pause 51]
This is the skill you'll use later: notice the number, and slow down early. Well done.
